name: Xining Caojiabao International Airport
before:
Qinghai's airport, on the Tibetan Plateau about 30 km east of Xining. It handled 7.88 million passengers in 2025 across 63,344 movements, both up around 12 per cent on the year.

Altitude and runway length go together here. A new 3,800 metre runway came into service in October 2011, and the original runway now works as a taxiway.

The airport opened in December 1991, replacing a field at Lejiawan 17 km to the west that had been built on the orders of the military governor Ma Bufang in 1931 and was still working off a one-way gravel runway in the 1970s. In the 1950s that older airport carried fewer than a thousand passengers a year on a route to Lanzhou, Baotou and Beijing. Its site is now a military base.
after:
The main airport for Qinghai, serving its capital, Xining, from about 30 km east of the city. It handled 7.88 million passengers in 2025 and 63,344 take-offs and landings, both up about 12 per cent on 2024.

Its single runway is 3,800 m long.
